questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के प्रति सबसे कम अभिक्रियाशील होगा ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following will be the least reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction ?

options.B: 4-मेथिलफेनिल क्लोराइड (Cl on aromatic ring, CH3 at para)

options_english.B: 4-Chlorotoluene (Cl directly on aromatic ring, CH3 at para)

questions.image_description: Four structural formulae: (A) benzyl chloride with CH2-Cl attached to benzene ring; (B) chlorobenzene with Cl directly on ring and CH3 at para position (4-chlorotoluene); (C) CH3-Cl; (D) chlorocyclohexane with Cl on the ring.
questions.solution: Option (B), 4-chlorotoluene, is the least reactive towards nucleophilic substitution because the chlorine atom is directly attached to the aromatic ring. The lone pairs on Cl are in conjugation with the pi system, making the C–Cl bond have partial double-bond character and thus very strong. This resonance stabilization prevents easy attack by a nucleophile. Benzyl chloride (A) is highly reactive because the resulting carbocation is stabilized by resonance with the ring. CH3Cl (C) and chlorocyclohexane (D) undergo normal SN2 reactions, but aryl halides like (B) are far less reactive.
questions.topic: Reactivity of halides towards nucleophilic substitution

questions.text: ऐल्कोहॉल के निर्जलन में सम्मिलित सबसे धीमे चरण के दौरान बनने वाला मध्यवर्ती है :
questions.text_english: The intermediate formed during the slowest step involved in the dehydration of alcohol is :
questions.solution: The dehydration of an alcohol in acid proceeds via an E1 mechanism. The alcohol first gets protonated (fast step) to form a protonated alcohol, which then loses water in the slow, rate-determining step to form a carbocation. This carbocation subsequently loses a proton to give the alkene. Therefore, the intermediate formed during the slowest step is a carbocation (option D). Carbanion (B) and free radical (C) are not involved; protonated alcohol (A) forms in the fast first step, not the slowest step.
questions.topic: Dehydration of alcohols, E1 mechanism

questions.text: [Co(en)3]2(SO4)3 में Co की ऑक्सीकरण संख्या है :
questions.text_english: The oxidation number of Co in [Co(en)3]2(SO4)3 is :
questions.solution: In [Co(en)3]2(SO4)3, ethylenediamine (en) is a neutral ligand, so it contributes 0 to the charge. The complex cation is [Co(en)3]^3+ and there are 3 sulphate ions each with charge -2, giving a total anion charge of -6. With 2 formula units of the complex, total positive charge = 6, so each complex cation has charge +3. Therefore, the oxidation number of Co is +3 (option A).
questions.topic: Oxidation number of central metal atom

questions.text: वर्नर के सिद्धान्त के अनुसार, केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु की प्राथमिक संयोजकताएँ :
questions.text_english: According to Werner's theory, the primary valencies of the central metal atom :

options.A: उदासीन अणुओं अथवा ऋणात्मक आयनों द्वारा संतुष्ट होती हैं।
options.B: उपसहसंयोजन संख्या के बराबर होती हैं।
options.C: ऋणात्मक आयनों से संतुष्ट होती हैं।

options_english.A: are satisfied by neutral molecules or negative ions.
options_english.B: are equal to its coordination number.

questions.solution: According to Werner's theory, the central metal atom has two types of valencies: primary (ionisable) and secondary (non-ionisable). Primary valencies are always satisfied by negative ions only — they are ionisable and appear outside the coordination sphere as counter ions. Secondary valencies, on the other hand, can be satisfied by both neutral molecules and negative ions, and are non-ionisable. Therefore, option (C) is correct. Option (A) describes secondary valencies, option (B) confuses primary valency with coordination number, and option (D) incorrectly says primary valencies are non-ionisable.
questions.topic: Werner's theory of coordination compounds

questions.text: (C2H5)2NH और (C2H5)3N के बीच विभेद करने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा अभिकर्मक प्रयुक्त होता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following reagent is used to distinguish between (C2H5)2NH and (C2H5)3N ?
questions.solution: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (C6H5SO2Cl), also known as Hinsberg's reagent, is used to distinguish between secondary and tertiary amines. Diethylamine (C2H5)2NH is a secondary amine; it reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to form a sulphonamide that is insoluble in alkali. Triethylamine (C2H5)3N is a tertiary amine; it does not react with Hinsberg's reagent because it has no N–H bond. This difference in reactivity clearly distinguishes the two. Hence, option (B) is correct.
questions.topic: Hinsberg's test, distinction between secondary and tertiary amines

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा प्रबलतम क्षारक है ?
questions.text_english: Among the following, which is the strongest base ?
questions.solution: Benzylamine (B), C6H5CH2NH2, is the strongest base among the four options. In benzylamine, the nitrogen lone pair is not directly in conjugation with the aromatic ring (the CH2 group acts as an insulator), so it is freely available for protonation. In aniline (D), 4-nitroaniline (A), and 4-methylaniline (C), the NH2 is directly attached to the ring; the lone pair is delocalized into the pi system, reducing basicity. The strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group in (A) further reduces electron density on nitrogen, making it the weakest base. Benzylamine behaves more like an aliphatic amine in terms of basicity.
questions.topic: Basicity of amines

questions.text: जलीय विलयन में, Cr2O7^2− आयन क्षारीय माध्यम में निम्नलिखित में से किसमें रूपांतरित हो जाता है ?
questions.text_english: In aqueous solution, Cr2O7^2− ion converts to which of the following in alkaline medium ?
questions.solution: Dichromate ion (Cr2O7^2−) is the stable form of chromium(VI) in acidic solution and appears orange in colour. In alkaline (basic) medium, it undergoes a reversible conversion to chromate ion (CrO4^2−), which is yellow in colour. The equilibrium is: Cr2O7^2− + 2OH^− ⇌ 2CrO4^2− + H2O. This interconversion is a simple acid-base equilibrium and does not involve any change in the oxidation state of chromium. Hence, option (B) is correct.
questions.topic: Chemistry of chromium, dichromate-chromate interconversion

questions.text: शुद्ध जल और एथेनॉल के क्वथनांकों की अपेक्षा जल और एथेनॉल के स्थिरक्वाथी मिश्रण का क्वथनांक कम होता है। यह मिश्रण दर्शाता है :
questions.text_english: The boiling point of an azeotropic mixture of water and ethanol is less than that of pure water and ethanol. The mixture shows :

options.A: राउल्ट के नियम से धनात्मक विचलन।
options.B: राउल्ट के नियम से ऋणात्मक विचलन।
options.C: राउल्ट के नियम से कोई विचलन नहीं।

options_english.D: that the solution is an ideal solution.

questions.solution: A minimum-boiling azeotrope has a boiling point lower than either of its pure components, which is a characteristic feature of solutions that show positive deviation from Raoult's law. In such solutions, the A–B intermolecular interactions are weaker than the A–A and B–B interactions present in the pure components. This leads to higher vapour pressures and a lower boiling point. The water–ethanol azeotrope (boiling at approximately 78.1°C) boils below both pure water (100°C) and pure ethanol (78.4°C). Hence option (A) is correct.
questions.topic: Azeotropes, deviation from Raoult's law

questions.text: किसी विलेय के 2·0 मोलल जलीय विलयन में उसका मोल-अंश होता है :
questions.text_english: The mole fraction of a solute in 2·0 molal aqueous solution is :
questions.solution: A 2.0 molal solution means 2.0 moles of solute per 1000 g of water. Moles of water = 1000/18 = 55.55 mol. Total moles = 2 + 55.55 = 57.55. Mole fraction of solute = 2/57.55 = 0.0347. Hence option (C) is correct. This calculation shows that even a 2 molal solution has a relatively small mole fraction of solute because water has a low molar mass and therefore a large number of moles per kilogram.
questions.topic: Concentration terms, mole fraction calculation

questions.text: प्लैटिनम इलेक्ट्रोडों के साथ NaCl के अति तनु जलीय विलयन का विद्युत-अपघटन करने पर :
questions.text_english: On electrolysis of very dilute aqueous solution of NaCl using platinum electrodes :

options.A: ऐनोड पर H2 गैस उत्सर्जित होती है।
options.B: कैथोड पर Na उत्पादित होता है।
options.C: ऐनोड पर O2 गैस उत्सर्जित होती है।
options.D: कैथोड पर H2 गैस उत्सर्जित होती है।

options_english.A: H2 gas is evolved at anode.
options_english.C: O2 gas is evolved at anode.
options_english.D: H2 gas is evolved at cathode.

questions.solution: In very dilute aqueous NaCl, both water and NaCl are present. At the cathode, H2O is preferentially reduced over Na+ (since Na+ reduction requires a very high negative potential and Na would immediately react with water), so H2 is evolved: 2H2O + 2e^− → H2 + 2OH^−. At the anode, in very dilute solution, Cl^− ions are present in very low concentration, so water is preferentially oxidised instead: 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e^−, giving O2 at the anode. Hence at cathode: H2; at anode: O2. The correct statement is (D) — H2 gas is evolved at cathode.
questions.topic: Electrolysis, products at electrodes

questions.text: किसी अभिक्रिया 3A → 2B के लिए, अभिक्रिया वेग +d[B]/dt बराबर है :
questions.text_english: For a reaction 3A → 2B, the rate of reaction +d[B]/dt is equal to :
questions.solution: For the reaction 3A → 2B, the rate of reaction is defined as: Rate = −(1/3) d[A]/dt = +(1/2) d[B]/dt. Therefore, d[B]/dt = (2/3)(−d[A]/dt) = −(2/3) d[A]/dt. The negative sign arises because [A] is decreasing while [B] is increasing. Option (B) gives −(2/3) d[A]/dt, which correctly expresses d[B]/dt in terms of the rate of disappearance of A.
questions.topic: Rate of reaction, stoichiometric relationship

questions.text: जल-अपघटन करने पर, निम्नलिखित कार्बोहाइड्रेटों में से कौन-सा केवल ग्लूकोस देता है ?
questions.text_english: On hydrolysis, which of the following carbohydrates gives only glucose ?
questions.solution: Maltose is a disaccharide formed by the condensation of two glucose units joined by an α-1,4-glycosidic linkage. On hydrolysis, it yields only glucose molecules. Sucrose (A) gives glucose + fructose on hydrolysis. Galactose (B) is a monosaccharide and does not undergo hydrolysis. Lactose (C) gives glucose + galactose on hydrolysis. Therefore, option (D) maltose is the correct answer.
questions.topic: Carbohydrates, hydrolysis of disaccharides

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : Zr और Hf का पृथक्करण कठिन होता है।
कारण (R) : क्योंकि Zr और Hf आवर्त सारणी के एक ही वर्ग के सदस्य हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Separation of Zr and Hf is difficult.
Reason (R) : Because Zr and Hf lie in the same group of the periodic table.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथनों के लिए सही कोड चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct code for the two statements.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the assertion and the reason are true. Separation of Zr and Hf is indeed extremely difficult, and it is also true that they belong to the same group (Group 4) of the periodic table. However, the reason does not correctly explain the assertion. The actual reason for the difficulty of separation is lanthanoid contraction: due to the filling of 4f orbitals before Hf, the atomic radius of Hf (156 pm) is almost equal to that of Zr (160 pm). This similarity in size leads to nearly identical chemical properties, making separation very difficult. Merely belonging to the same group does not, by itself, explain the difficulty — many same-group pairs can be easily separated. Hence option (B) is correct.
questions.topic: Lanthanoid contraction, separation of Zr and Hf

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : 4-मेथिलफीनॉल की अपेक्षा फीनॉल कम अम्लीय है।
कारण (R) : फीनॉल में इलेक्ट्रॉन विमोचक समूह की उपस्थिति इसको कम अम्लीय कर देती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Phenol is less acidic than 4-methylphenol.
Reason (R) : The presence of an electron releasing group in phenol makes it less acidic.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथनों के लिए सही कोड चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct code for the two statements.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The assertion is false: phenol is actually MORE acidic than 4-methylphenol, not less. This is because the methyl group in 4-methylphenol is an electron-donating group that increases electron density on the phenoxide oxygen, destabilising the conjugate base and reducing acidity. The reason stated is correct in general — an electron-releasing group does make a phenol less acidic — and this is why 4-methylphenol is less acidic than phenol, not the other way around. Since assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true, option (D) is the correct answer.
questions.topic: Acidic nature of phenols, effect of substituents

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : गैब्रिएल थैलिमाइड संश्लेषण द्वारा ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक ऐमीनों का विरचन नहीं किया जा सकता है।
कारण (R) : गैब्रिएल थैलिमाइड संश्लेषण का प्रयोग प्राथमिक ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीनों के विरचन के लिए किया जाता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.
Reason (R) : Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथनों के लिए सही कोड चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct code for the two statements.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason properly explains the assertion. Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves the alkylation of potassium phthalimide with an alkyl halide, followed by hydrolysis. Aryl halides do not undergo this nucleophilic substitution reaction (they are too unreactive towards SN2 attack by phthalimide anion), so aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by this method. The synthesis is specifically used for making primary aliphatic amines, which correctly explains why aromatic amines are excluded. Hence, option (A) is correct.
questions.topic: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : अभिक्रिया की कोटि प्राथमिक एवं जटिल दोनों प्रकार की अभिक्रियाओं पर लागू होती है।
कारण (R) : अभिक्रिया की कोटि एक प्रायोगिक मात्रा है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Order of reaction is applicable to elementary as well as complex reactions.
Reason (R) : Order of a reaction is an experimental quantity.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथनों के लिए सही कोड चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct code for the two statements.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both assertion and reason are correct, and reason correctly explains the assertion. Order of a reaction is determined experimentally from the rate law: Rate = k[A]^m[B]^n, where m and n are found by experiment. Because it is an experimentally determined quantity (not derived from stoichiometry), it can be applied to both elementary and complex (multi-step) reactions, and can even be fractional or zero. Molecularity, in contrast, applies only to elementary reactions and is always a whole number. Hence option (A) is correct.
questions.topic: Order of reaction vs molecularity

questions.text: C4H9Br अणुसूत्र वाले यौगिक के लिए, लिखिए :
questions.text_english: For the compound having molecular formula C4H9Br, write :

sub_questions.text: समावयव जो SN1 प्रतिस्थापन के प्रति सर्वाधिक अभिक्रियाशील है।
sub_questions.text_english: The isomer which is most reactive towards SN1 displacement.

key_points: (CH3)3CBr — 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tertiary butyl bromide) is most reactive towards SN1 because it forms the most stable tertiary carbocation intermediate.

sub_questions.solution: The isomer most reactive towards SN1 is (CH3)3CBr, i.e., 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tertiary butyl bromide). In the SN1 mechanism, the rate-determining step is the ionisation of the C–X bond to form a carbocation. A tertiary carbocation (CH3)3C+ is stabilised by three electron-donating methyl groups through hyperconjugation and inductive effects, making it the most stable and easiest to form. Therefore, this isomer undergoes SN1 reaction most readily.

sub_questions.text: समावयव जो शुष्क ईथर की उपस्थिति में Na धातु के साथ अभिक्रिया करके 2,5-डाइमेथिलहैक्सेन देता है।
sub_questions.text_english: The isomer which, on reacting with Na metal in the presence of dry ether, gives 2,5-Dimethylhexane.

key_points: (CH3)2CHCH2Br — 1-bromo-2-methylpropane (isobutyl bromide). Two molecules couple in Wurtz reaction to give 2,5-dimethylhexane.

sub_questions.solution: The Wurtz reaction involves coupling of two alkyl halide molecules in the presence of Na metal and dry ether: 2 RX + 2Na → R–R + 2NaX. 2,5-Dimethylhexane has the structure (CH3)2CHCH2CH2CH(CH3)2. This is formed by coupling two molecules of (CH3)2CHCH2Br (isobutyl bromide, or 1-bromo-2-methylpropane). Hence the required isomer is (CH3)2CHCH2Br, i.e., 1-bromo-2-methylpropane.

questions.solution: Answers are provided in sub-questions (a) and (b) above.
questions.topic: Isomers of C4H9Br, SN1 reactivity, Wurtz reaction

questions.text:
अभिक्रिया A + B → उत्पाद के लिए, वेग नियम है : वेग = k[A][B]^(3/2)
अभिक्रिया की समग्र कोटि लिखिए। क्या यह अभिक्रिया एक प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया हो सकती है? अपने उत्तर के समर्थन के लिए कारण दीजिए।
questions.text_english:
For a reaction A + B → Products, the rate law is : Rate = k[A][B]^(3/2)
Write the overall order of the reaction. Can this reaction be an elementary reaction ? Give reason in support of your answer.

key_points: Overall order = 1 + 3/2 = 5/2 (2.5)
This cannot be an elementary reaction because elementary reactions have molecularity as a whole number, and their order equals their molecularity.

questions.solution: The overall order of the reaction is 1 + 3/2 = 5/2 = 2.5. This reaction cannot be an elementary reaction. For an elementary reaction, the order of each reactant must equal its stoichiometric coefficient in the balanced equation, and the overall order must be a small positive whole number (1, 2, or 3 at most). Here the order with respect to B is 3/2, which is a fraction. Elementary reactions must have whole-number orders because their rate is directly proportional to the number of colliding molecules. A fractional order indicates a complex (multi-step) mechanism, not a single-step elementary process.
questions.topic: Order of reaction, elementary vs complex reactions

questions.text: व्याख्या कीजिए कि क्यों 1 लीटर जल में 1 मोल KCl मिलाने पर जल का क्वथनांक बढ़ जाता है, जबकि 1 लीटर जल में 1 मोल मेथिल ऐल्कोहॉल मिलाने पर जल का क्वथनांक घट जाता है।
questions.text_english: Explain why, on addition of 1 mol of KCl to 1 litre of water, the boiling point of water increases, while the addition of 1 mol of methyl alcohol to 1 litre of water decreases the boiling point.

key_points: KCl is a non-volatile electrolyte that elevates boiling point (colligative property — elevation of boiling point).
Methyl alcohol is a volatile solute; it forms an azeotrope with water showing positive deviation, leading to a lower boiling point.

questions.solution: When 1 mol of KCl is dissolved in water, it dissociates into K+ and Cl− ions, effectively giving 2 moles of solute particles. KCl is a non-volatile solute, so it reduces the vapour pressure of water (Raoult's law). This results in elevation of boiling point, which is a colligative property. When 1 mol of methyl alcohol is dissolved in water, methanol is a volatile solute. The water–methanol mixture shows positive deviation from Raoult's law because the intermolecular attractions between water and methanol are weaker than in the pure liquids. This increases the total vapour pressure above the ideal value, and consequently the boiling point of the mixture decreases below that of pure water.
questions.topic: Elevation of boiling point, deviation from Raoult's law

key_points: A ligand that can coordinate to the central metal through two different donor atoms is called an ambidentate ligand. Example: NO2^− (nitrite) can coordinate through N (nitro, -NO2) or through O (nitrito, -ONO).

sub_questions.solution: An ambidentate ligand is one that has two different donor atoms through either of which it can coordinate to the central metal atom, forming different linkage isomers. For example, the nitrite ion (NO2^−) can bond to a metal through its nitrogen atom (forming nitro complexes, written as -NO2) or through one of its oxygen atoms (forming nitrito complexes, written as -ONO). Another example is the thiocyanate ion (SCN^−), which can coordinate through sulphur or nitrogen.

key_points: A double salt is formed by the combination of two different salts in a stoichiometric ratio and loses its identity in solution. Example: Mohr's salt, FeSO4.(NH4)2SO4.6H2O.

sub_questions.solution: A double salt is a compound formed when two simple salts crystallise together in a definite molar ratio. In solution, a double salt dissociates completely into its constituent ions, losing its distinct identity. A classic example is Mohr's salt, FeSO4·(NH4)2SO4·6H2O, which in aqueous solution simply gives Fe2+, NH4+, and SO4^2− ions separately. This distinguishes it from a complex salt, where the complex ion retains its identity in solution.

key_points: Glucose on treatment with HI for a prolonged time gives n-hexane, showing that all six carbon atoms are in a straight (unbranched) chain.

sub_questions.solution: The presence of a straight chain in glucose is established by the fact that on prolonged treatment with concentrated HI, glucose gives n-hexane as the only hydrocarbon product. questions.text:
किसी रेडियोसक्रिय तत्त्व की अर्द्ध-आयु 1·5 × 10^10 वर्ष है। उस समय का परिकलन कीजिए जिसमें तत्त्व की सक्रियता उसके प्रारंभिक मान से घटकर 75% रह जाती है।
[दिया गया है: log 2 = 0·30, log 3 = 0·48, log 4 = 0·60]
questions.text_english:
The half-life period of a radioactive element is 1·5 × 10^10 years. Calculate the time in which the activity of the element is reduced to 75% of its original value.
[Given : log 2 = 0·30, log 3 = 0·48, log 4 = 0·60]
questions.solution:
Given: t1/2 = 1.5 × 10^10 years. Activity reduced to 75% means N/N0 = 0.75 = 3/4, so N0/N = 4/3.

The decay constant: λ = 0.693 / t1/2 = 0.693 / (1.5 × 10^10) yr^−1.

Using: t = (2.303 / λ) × log(N0/N) = (2.303 × t1/2 / 0.693) × log(4/3).

log(4/3) = log 4 − log 3 = 0.60 − 0.48 = 0.12.

t = (2.303 × 1.5 × 10^10 / 0.693) × 0.12
= (2.303 / 0.693) × 1.5 × 10^10 × 0.12
= 3.323 × 1.5 × 10^10 × 0.12
= 3.323 × 0.18 × 10^10
= 0.5981 × 10^10
≈ 6.0 × 10^9 years.

Therefore, the time required for the activity to reduce to 75% of its initial value is approximately 6.0 × 10^9 years (about 6 billion years).
questions.topic: Radioactive decay, half-life calculations

questions.text: आयनों के स्वतंत्र अभिगमन का कोलराउश का नियम बताइए। एक वक्र की सहायता से व्याख्या कीजिए कि दुर्बल विद्युत-अपघट्यों के लिए सांद्रता − मोलर चालकता वक्र के बहिर्वेशन द्वारा Λ°m का मान ज्ञात क्यों नहीं किया जा सकता है, जिस प्रकार प्रबल विद्युत-अपघट्यों के लिए किया जा सकता है।
questions.text_english: State Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions. With the help of a curve, explain why it is not easy to determine Λ°m for weak electrolytes by extrapolating the concentration − molar conductivity curve, as it is for strong electrolytes.

key_points: Kohlrausch's law: Λ°m = ν+ λ°+ + ν− λ°−

For strong electrolytes, the Λm vs √c plot is linear and can be extrapolated to zero concentration. For weak electrolytes the plot is not linear near zero concentration and rises sharply, making extrapolation unreliable.

questions.solution:
Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions states that at infinite dilution, the molar conductivity of an electrolyte is equal to the sum of the molar conductivities of its individual ions: Λ°m = ν+ λ°+ + ν− λ°−, where ν+ and ν− are the number of cations and anions per formula unit, and λ°+ and λ°− are their limiting molar ionic conductivities.

For strong electrolytes, the plot of Λm versus √c is nearly linear (Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation), so it can be easily extrapolated to zero concentration (√c = 0) to obtain Λ°m.

For weak electrolytes (e.g., acetic acid), the degree of dissociation is very small at higher concentrations but increases sharply as concentration approaches zero. As a result, the Λm versus √c curve is not linear — it rises steeply and almost vertically near zero concentration. Extrapolation of such a steep curve is not reliable and cannot give an accurate value of Λ°m. Therefore, Kohlrausch's law is used instead to calculate Λ°m of weak electrolytes indirectly from the known Λ°m values of related strong electrolytes.
questions.topic: Kohlrausch's law, molar conductivity of weak and strong electrolytes

questions.text:
31 g एथिलीन ग्लाइकॉल (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 62 g mol^−1) को 600 g जल में घोलकर एक प्रतिहिम विलयन बनाया जाता है। विलयन का हिमांक परिकलित कीजिए।
(जल के लिए Kf = 1·86 K kg mol^−1)
questions.text_english: An antifreeze solution is prepared by dissolving 31 g of ethylene glycol (Molar mass = 62 g mol^−1) in 600 g of water. Calculate the freezing point of the solution. (Kf for water = 1·86 K kg mol^−1)

key_points: Moles of ethylene glycol = 31/62 = 0.5 mol
Molality = 0.5 / 0.6 = 0.833 mol kg^−1
Freezing point = 0 − 1.55 = −1.55°C

questions.solution:
Step 1: Moles of ethylene glycol (solute) = mass / molar mass = 31 / 62 = 0.5 mol.

Step 2: Mass of solvent (water) = 600 g = 0.6 kg.

Step 3: Molality (m) = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg = 0.5 / 0.6 = 0.833 mol kg^−1.

Step 4: Depression in freezing point: ΔTf = Kf × m = 1.86 × 0.833 = 1.549 ≈ 1.55 K.

Step 5: Freezing point of solution = 0°C − 1.55°C = −1.55°C.

Therefore, the freezing point of the antifreeze solution is −1.55°C.
questions.topic: Depression of freezing point, colligative properties

sub_questions.text: प्रत्येक प्रकरण में सम्मिलित संकरण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the hybridization involved in each case for [NiCl4]^2− and [Ni(CN)4]^2−.

key_points: [NiCl4]^2−: sp3 hybridisation (tetrahedral); [Ni(CN)4]^2−: dsp2 hybridisation (square planar)

sub_questions.solution: Ni has atomic number 28, electronic configuration [Ar] 3d^8 4s^2. In Ni^2+, the configuration is 3d^8. Cl^− is a weak field ligand so it does not cause pairing of 3d electrons; the complex [NiCl4]^2− is tetrahedral with sp3 hybridisation. CN^− is a strong field ligand that causes pairing of electrons in the 3d orbitals, making one 3d orbital empty; the complex [Ni(CN)4]^2− is square planar with dsp2 hybridisation (using one 3d, one 4s, and two 4p orbitals).

sub_questions.text: इनमें से कौन-सा आंतरिक कक्षक संकुल है और कौन-सा बाह्य कक्षक संकुल है?
sub_questions.text_english: Which of them is the inner orbital complex and which is the outer orbital complex?

key_points: [Ni(CN)4]^2− is the inner orbital complex (uses 3d orbital for hybridisation); [NiCl4]^2− is the outer orbital complex (uses only 4s and 4p orbitals).

sub_questions.solution: [Ni(CN)4]^2− is the inner orbital complex because it uses an inner d orbital (3d) in its dsp2 hybridisation. [NiCl4]^2− is the outer orbital complex because its sp3 hybridisation uses only the 4s and 4p orbitals (outer orbitals), with all 3d orbitals remaining untouched.

sub_questions.text: इनके चुम्बकीय व्यवहार की तुलना कीजिए।

key_points: [NiCl4]^2− is paramagnetic (2 unpaired electrons); [Ni(CN)4]^2− is diamagnetic (0 unpaired electrons).

sub_questions.solution: [NiCl4]^2− has sp3 hybridisation with Ni^2+ retaining the 3d^8 configuration with two unpaired electrons (Cl^− is a weak field ligand, no pairing occurs). Hence it is paramagnetic. [Ni(CN)4]^2− has dsp2 hybridisation; CN^− is a strong field ligand that forces the pairing of all 3d electrons, resulting in no unpaired electrons. Hence it is diamagnetic.

sub_questions.text: जैव तंत्र में महत्त्वपूर्ण दो उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के नाम लिखिए।

key_points: Haemoglobin (iron-porphyrin complex) and Chlorophyll (magnesium-porphyrin complex)

sub_questions.solution: Two important coordination compounds in biological systems are: (1) Haemoglobin — a coordination compound of iron(II) with a porphyrin ring (haem), present in red blood cells and responsible for transport of oxygen in the blood. (2) Chlorophyll — a coordination compound of magnesium with a porphyrin ring, present in plants and essential for photosynthesis.

sub_questions.text: कीलेट प्रभाव से क्या अभिप्राय है? एक उदाहरण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: What is meant by chelate effect ? Give an example.

key_points: The chelate effect refers to the extra stability of complexes containing chelate rings (formed by polydentate ligands) compared to analogous complexes with unidentate ligands. Example: [Ni(en)3]^2+ is more stable than [Ni(NH3)6]^2+.

sub_questions.solution: The chelate effect refers to the enhanced stability of a coordination complex when polydentate (chelating) ligands form ring structures (chelate rings) with the central metal atom compared to the corresponding complex with an equivalent number of monodentate ligands. This extra stability arises from a favourable entropy contribution: when a polydentate ligand replaces several monodentate ligands, the number of free particles in solution increases, increasing the entropy of the system. For example, [Ni(en)3]^2+ (where en is ethylenediamine, a bidentate ligand) is considerably more stable than [Ni(NH3)6]^2+.

sub_questions.text: निम्न प्रचलन चतुष्फलकीय संकुल विरलेही क्यों बनते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are low spin tetrahedral complexes rarely formed ?

key_points: The crystal field splitting energy (Δt) in tetrahedral complexes is only about 4/9 Δo, which is much smaller than in octahedral complexes, so it is rarely large enough to overcome the pairing energy and force electron pairing.

sub_questions.solution: In tetrahedral complexes, the crystal field splitting energy (Δt) is only about 4/9 of the octahedral splitting energy (Δo) for the same metal and same ligands. This is because in tetrahedral geometry only four ligands are present and none of them are directed straight at any d orbital. Since Δt is always much smaller than the pairing energy (P) for most ligands, it is not energetically favourable for electrons to be forced into paired configurations. Therefore, low spin configurations are rarely achieved in tetrahedral complexes, and most tetrahedral complexes are high spin.

(ग) क्लोरोफॉर्म का संग्रहण बन्द गहरी रंगीन बोतलों में किया जाता है।
questions.text_english:
Give reasons for the following :
(a) Although chlorine is an electron-withdrawing group, yet it is ortho-, para-directing in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions.
(b) Aryl halides cannot be prepared by reacting phenol with concentrated halogen acids or phosphorus halides.
(c) Chloroform is stored in closed dark coloured bottles.

key_points: (a) Cl withdraws electrons by inductive effect (−I) but donates through resonance (+M), making ortho/para positions electron-rich.
(b) The C–O bond in phenol has partial double bond character due to resonance; it is too strong to be cleaved by HX or PX3.
(c) CHCl3 oxidises in air and light to toxic phosgene (COCl2); dark bottles prevent photochemical oxidation.

questions.solution:
(a) Chlorine is electron-withdrawing by the inductive effect (−I effect) due to its high electronegativity, but it is electron-donating by resonance (+M effect) because it can donate one of its lone pairs to the aromatic ring. The +M effect dominates the directing influence, making the ortho and para positions electron-rich. Therefore, despite being weakly deactivating overall (due to the dominant −I effect), chlorine directs the incoming electrophile to ortho and para positions.

(b) In phenol, the C–O bond has partial double bond character due to resonance of the lone pair on oxygen with the aromatic ring. This makes the C–O bond shorter and stronger than in ordinary alcohols. As a result, concentrated halogen acids (HX) or phosphorus halides (PX3/PX5) — which normally protonate the OH and then cleave the C–O bond — cannot cleave this unusually strong C–O bond. Hence aryl halides cannot be prepared from phenol by these reagents.

(c) Chloroform (CHCl3) is readily oxidised by atmospheric oxygen in the presence of light to form phosgene (COCl2), a highly toxic gas: 2CHCl3 + O2 → 2COCl2 + 2HCl. To prevent this oxidation, chloroform is stored in closed, dark-coloured bottles that exclude both light and air.
questions.chapter: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes / Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.topic: Directing effects, aryl halide preparation, stability of chloroform

(ख) बेन्जीन

questions.text_english:
How will you obtain the following from benzenediazonium chloride ? Give chemical equations involved :
(a) Chlorobenzene
(b) Benzene
(c) Benzonitrile

key_points: (a) Sandmeyer reaction: C6H5N2+Cl− + CuCl/HCl → C6H5Cl + N2
(b) C6H5N2+Cl− + H3PO2 + H2O → C6H6 + N2 + HCl + H3PO3 (Hypophosphorous acid reduction)
(c) Sandmeyer reaction: C6H5N2+Cl− + CuCN → C6H5CN + N2

questions.solution:
(a) Chlorobenzene: Benzenediazonium chloride is treated with cuprous chloride (CuCl) in hydrochloric acid (Sandmeyer reaction):
C6H5N2+Cl− + CuCl/HCl → C6H5Cl + N2 + CuCl

(b) Benzene: Benzenediazonium chloride is treated with hypophosphorous acid (H3PO2) in the presence of water (a diazonium salt reduction that replaces −N2+ with H):
C6H5N2+Cl− + H3PO2 + H2O → C6H6 + N2 + H3PO3 + HCl

(c) Benzonitrile: Benzenediazonium chloride is treated with cuprous cyanide (CuCN) (Sandmeyer reaction):

questions.text: C3H5N आण्विक सूत्र का एक कार्बनिक यौगिक (A), C6H5MgBr के साथ अभिक्रिया करने के उपरान्त जल-अपघटन करने पर यौगिक (B) देता है। यौगिक (B), 2,4-डी.एन.पी. अभिकर्मक के साथ नारंगी-लाल अवक्षेप देता है तथा आयोडोफॉर्म परीक्षण नहीं देता है। यह टॉलेन्स अभिकर्मक अथवा फेलिंग अभिकर्मक को अपचित नहीं करता है और न ही ब्रोमीन जल को वर्णविहीन करता है। यह क्रोमिक अम्ल द्वारा प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण से एक कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल (C) बनाता है जिसका आण्विक सूत्र C7H6O2 है। यौगिक (A), (B) और (C) को पहचानिए। यौगिक (A) की C6H5MgBr के साथ अभिक्रिया करने के उपरान्त जल-अपघटन करने पर यौगिक (B) बनने की अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए।
questions.text_english: An organic compound (A) with molecular formula C3H5N on reaction with C6H5MgBr followed by hydrolysis, gives a compound (B). Compound (B) forms an orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and does not give iodoform test. It neither reduces Tollens' or Fehling's reagent nor does it decolourise bromine water. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid it gives a carboxylic acid (C) having molecular formula C7H6O2. Identify the compounds (A), (B) and (C). Write the reactions of compound (A) with C6H5MgBr followed by hydrolysis to give compound (B).

key_points: (A) = CH2=CH–CN (acrylonitrile / propenenitrile)

(B) = C6H5–CO–CH2CH3 or more precisely: C6H5COCH=CH2 — actually (B) is C6H5–CO–CH2CH3 phenyl vinyl ketone... Let us recalculate: A is C3H5N = CH2=CHCN. Reaction with PhMgBr then hydrolysis: nitrile + RMgBr → ketone. CH2=CH-CN + C6H5MgBr → after hydrolysis → C6H5COCH=CH2 (phenyl vinyl ketone/1-phenylbut-2-en-1-one? No: CH2=CH-CN + C6H5MgBr → CH2=CH-C(=NMgBr)Ph → H3O+ → CH2=CHCOC6H5 = phenyl vinyl ketone, C9H8O. B gives 2,4-DNP (ketone), no iodoform (no CH3CO), no Tollens/Fehling (not aldehyde). Drastic oxidation of C=C and Ph gives benzoic acid C7H6O2. All consistent.
(C) = C6H5COOH (benzoic acid)

questions.solution:
Identification: Compound (A) is CH2=CH−CN (acrylonitrile, propenenitrile), molecular formula C3H5N.

Reaction: When a nitrile (RCN) reacts with a Grignard reagent (R'MgX) and the product is hydrolysed, a ketone is obtained. Thus:
CH2=CH−CN + C6H5MgBr → [CH2=CH−C(=NMgBr)−C6H5] → H3O+ → CH2=CH−CO−C6H5 + NH3

Compound (B) is phenyl vinyl ketone (1-phenylprop-2-en-1-one), C9H8O.

Verification: (B) gives orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNP (confirms carbonyl group/ketone); does not give iodoform test (no CH3CO− group); does not reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagent (confirms it is a ketone, not an aldehyde); does not decolourise bromine water (the C=C is conjugated and less reactive). On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, both the vinyl group and the ring side chain are oxidised, giving benzoic acid (C6H5COOH), molecular formula C7H6O2.

Compound (C) is benzoic acid, C7H6O2.

questions.text: जैव-तंत्र अनेक जटिल जैव अणुओं जैसे कार्बोहाइड्रेट, प्रोटीन, न्यूक्लिक अम्ल, लिपिड, आदि से मिलकर बनते हैं। प्रोटीन और कार्बोहाइड्रेट हमारे भोजन के आवश्यक अवयव हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त कुछ सरल अणु जैसे विटामिन और खनिज लवण भी जीवों की कार्य-प्रणालियों में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं। सभी प्रोटीन α-ऐमीनो अम्लों के बहुलक होते हैं। आण्विक आकृति के आधार पर प्रोटीनों को दो वर्गों में वर्गीकृत किया जा सकता है — रेशेदार प्रोटीन और गोलिकाकार प्रोटीन। विटामिन आहार में आवश्यक सहायक भोज्य कारक हैं। इन्हें वसा-विलेय तथा जल-विलेय में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है। विटामिनों की कमी से अनेक रोग हो जाते हैं। न्यूक्लिक अम्ल न्यूक्लियोटाइडों के बहुलक हैं जो एक क्षारक, एक पेन्टोस शर्करा तथा एक फॉस्फेट अवशांश से मिलकर बनते हैं। न्यूक्लिक अम्ल दो प्रकार के होते हैं — DNA और RNA। न्यूक्लिक अम्ल जनक से संतति में गुणों के स्थानांतरण के लिए जिम्मेदार होते हैं।
questions.text_english: Living systems are made up of various complex biomolecules like carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, etc. Proteins and carbohydrates are essential constituents of our food. In addition, some simple molecules like vitamins and mineral salts also play an important role in the functions of organisms. All proteins are polymers of α-amino acids. Proteins can be classified into two types on the basis of their molecular shape — Fibrous and Globular proteins. Vitamins are accessory food factors required in the diet. They are classified as fat-soluble and water-soluble. Deficiency of vitamins leads to many diseases. sub_questions.text_english: Write the name of basic building units of proteins and nucleic acids. How can you differentiate between Fibrous and Globular proteins on the basis of their structures ?

key_points: Basic unit of proteins = α-amino acids; basic unit of nucleic acids = nucleotides
Fibrous proteins: polypeptide chains run parallel and are held by hydrogen/disulphide bonds forming fibres; they are insoluble in water. E.g., keratin, myosin.
Globular proteins: polypeptide chains are coiled and folded into a spherical (globular) shape; generally soluble in water. E.g., insulin, haemoglobin.

sub_questions.solution: The basic building unit (monomer) of proteins is α-amino acids, and the basic building unit of nucleic acids is nucleotides. Fibrous proteins have polypeptide chains aligned parallel to each other, held together by hydrogen bonds and disulphide linkages along the length of the chain, forming long, fibre-like structures. They are generally insoluble in water and serve structural roles (e.g., keratin in hair and nails, collagen in tendons). Globular proteins have polypeptide chains that are folded and coiled into compact, spherical (globular) shapes through various intramolecular bonds. They are generally soluble in water and carry out dynamic functions such as catalysis and transport (e.g., haemoglobin, insulin).

key_points: Products: Thymine (nitrogenous base) + 2-deoxyribose (pentose sugar) + phosphoric acid

sub_questions.solution: When a nucleotide from DNA containing thymine is hydrolysed, three products are obtained: (1) Thymine — the nitrogenous base (a pyrimidine base); (2) 2-Deoxyribose — the pentose sugar present in DNA (as opposed to ribose in RNA); and (3) Phosphoric acid (H3PO4) — the phosphate moiety. These three components are the fundamental parts of any nucleotide.

sub_questions.text_english: Write one structural difference between DNA and RNA.

key_points: DNA contains 2-deoxyribose sugar and the base thymine; RNA contains ribose sugar and the base uracil instead of thymine.

sub_questions.solution: One structural difference between DNA and RNA is the sugar component: DNA contains 2-deoxyribose (a pentose sugar lacking an OH group at the 2' position), while RNA contains ribose (which has an OH group at the 2' position). Additionally, DNA contains the base thymine (5-methyluracil), whereas RNA contains uracil in its place.

questions.text_english: Alcohols have higher boiling points than other compounds, namely hydrocarbons, ethers and haloalkanes of comparable molecular masses. On oxidation, primary alcohols yield aldehydes with mild oxidizing agents and carboxylic acids with strong oxidizing agents. Secondary alcohols yield ketones on oxidation while tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation. Ethers may be prepared by dehydration of alcohols and Williamson synthesis. The C−O bond in ethers can be cleaved by hydrogen halides. sub_questions.solution: (i) To oxidise a primary alcohol to an aldehyde (without further oxidation to the acid), a mild oxidising agent is used: Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC, C5H5NH+CrO3Cl−) is the most common reagent. sub_questions.text_english: Write the reaction involved in Kolbe's reaction.

key_points: Phenol + NaOH → sodium phenoxide; sodium phenoxide + CO2 (under pressure, ~125°C) → sodium salicylate; sodium salicylate + HCl → salicylic acid

sub_questions.solution:
In Kolbe's reaction, phenol is first treated with NaOH to form sodium phenoxide (C6H5O^−Na+). Sodium phenoxide is then heated with carbon dioxide under high pressure (about 4–7 atm) at 125°C, forming sodium salicylate (sodium 2-hydroxybenzoate). On acidification with HCl, salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) is obtained:
C6H5OH + NaOH → C6H5ONa + H2O
C6H5ONa + CO2 → (at 125°C, pressure) → HOC6H4COONa (sodium salicylate)
HOC6H4COONa + HCl → HOC6H4COOH + NaCl

sub_questions.text_english: Why are tertiary alcohols resistant to oxidation ?

key_points: Tertiary alcohols have no α-hydrogen atom (the carbon bearing OH has no H attached to it), so the oxidation mechanism (which requires removal of an α-H) cannot proceed.

sub_questions.solution: Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation because in the oxidation mechanism of alcohols, the oxidising agent must abstract an α-hydrogen atom (the hydrogen on the carbon bearing the −OH group). In tertiary alcohols, the carbon atom attached to the −OH group bears no hydrogen atom — it is bonded to three other carbon groups. Therefore, the oxidising agent cannot abstract the required α-H, and oxidation does not occur under normal conditions.

Products: 2-iodo-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl iodide) and ethanol.

sub_questions.text: Fe अथवा Cu − उच्चतर गलनांक
sub_questions.text_english: Fe or Cu − higher melting point

key_points: Fe has a higher melting point (1535°C) than Cu (1083°C) because Fe has more unpaired d-electrons contributing to stronger metallic bonding.

sub_questions.solution: Fe has a higher melting point (approximately 1535°C) compared to Cu (approximately 1083°C). Iron has more unpaired d-electrons ([Ar] 3d^6 4s^2 → 4 unpaired in d, contributing 2 from 4s) that participate in metallic bonding, resulting in a stronger metal lattice. Copper ([Ar] 3d^10 4s^1) has a completely filled d-subshell with minimal d-electron participation in metallic bonding, giving it a weaker lattice and lower melting point.

sub_questions.text: Ti^3+ अथवा Sc^3+ − जलीय विलयन में रंगीन
sub_questions.text_english: Ti^3+ or Sc^3+ − coloured in aqueous solution

key_points: Ti^3+ is coloured (violet) in aqueous solution because it has one unpaired d-electron (d^1) enabling d-d transitions. Sc^3+ has no d-electrons (d^0) and is colourless.

sub_questions.solution: Ti^3+ is coloured (violet) in aqueous solution. Sc has the configuration [Ar] 3d^1 4s^2; upon forming Sc^3+, all three outer electrons are lost, giving a d^0 configuration. With no d-electrons, d-d transitions are impossible, so Sc^3+ is colourless. Ti has configuration [Ar] 3d^2 4s^2; Ti^3+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d^1, with one unpaired d-electron. This single electron can undergo a d-d transition when it absorbs visible light, making Ti^3+ coloured (violet/purple) in aqueous solution.

sub_questions.text: Cr अथवा Zn − उच्चतर तृतीय आयनन एन्थैल्पी
sub_questions.text_english: Cr or Zn − higher third ionisation enthalpy

key_points: Zn has higher third ionisation enthalpy because Zn^2+ has a completely filled 3d^10 configuration, which is highly stable. Removal of the third electron requires disruption of this stable filled subshell, requiring much more energy.

sub_questions.solution: Zinc (Zn) has a higher third ionisation enthalpy than chromium (Cr). Cr has the configuration [Ar] 3d^5 4s^1; after losing two electrons, Cr^2+ has a 3d^4 configuration from which the third electron can be removed with moderate energy. Zn has the configuration [Ar] 3d^10 4s^2; after losing two electrons, Zn^2+ has a completely filled 3d^10 configuration — which is an exceptionally stable configuration. Removing the third electron from this very stable, filled d-subshell requires an extremely large amount of energy. Hence Zn has a much higher third ionisation enthalpy than Cr.

sub_questions.text: अम्लीय माध्यम में MnO4^− की निम्नलिखित के साथ ऑक्सीकारक क्रिया के लिए आयनिक समीकरण लिखिए : (I) Fe^2+ आयन (II) I^− आयन

sub_questions.solution:
In acidic medium, permanganate (MnO4^−) acts as a powerful oxidising agent, being reduced to Mn^2+.

(I) With Fe^2+ ions:

(Fe^2+ is oxidised to Fe^3+; Mn goes from +7 to +2)

(II) With I^− ions:
2MnO4^− + 10I^− + 16H^+ → 2Mn^2+ + 5I2 + 8H2O

key_points: CH3−C(=N−NH−CO−NH2)−CH3 — acetone semicarbazone

sub_questions.solution:
Acetone reacts with semicarbazide (H2N−NH−CO−NH2) to form acetone semicarbazone via nucleophilic addition-elimination:
CH3COCH3 + H2N−NH−CO−NH2 → CH3C(=N−NH−CO−NH2)CH3 + H2O
The structure of acetone semicarbazone is: CH3−C(=N−NHCONH2)−CH3, i.e., a C=N bond with the semicarbazide group attached.

sub_questions.text_english: Why are α-hydrogen atoms of aldehydes and ketones acidic in nature ?

key_points: The α-hydrogen is acidic because the carbanion formed after its removal is stabilised by resonance with the C=O group (enolate ion formation).

sub_questions.solution: The α-hydrogen atoms of aldehydes and ketones are acidic because when an α-H is removed by a base, the resulting carbanion (enolate ion) is stabilised by resonance with the adjacent carbonyl (C=O) group. The negative charge is delocalised between the α-carbon and the oxygen atom of the carbonyl group, forming a resonance-stabilised enolate anion. This stabilisation of the conjugate base makes the α-H easier to remove and therefore acidic in character.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनकी HCN के प्रति अभिक्रियाशीलता के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए : CH3COCH3, CH3CHO, (CH3)3C−CO−CH3
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN : CH3COCH3, CH3CHO, (CH3)3C−CO−CH3

key_points: Increasing order of reactivity: (CH3)3CCOCH3 < CH3COCH3 < CH3CHO

sub_questions.solution: Reactivity towards HCN (nucleophilic addition) depends on two factors: (1) the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon — more positive charge = more reactive; (2) steric hindrance around the carbonyl carbon — more bulky groups = less reactive. Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones because they have only one electron-donating alkyl group and less steric hindrance. Among ketones, more bulky substituents reduce reactivity. Order of increasing reactivity towards HCN: (CH3)3C−CO−CH3 < CH3COCH3 < CH3CHO.

key_points: Toluene + CrO2Cl2 (chromyl chloride) → chromium complex → H3O+ → benzaldehyde

sub_questions.solution:
In the Etard reaction, toluene (or a methyl-substituted benzene) is treated with chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) in carbon disulphide (CS2) to form a brown chromium complex intermediate. On hydrolysis of this complex with water, benzaldehyde is obtained:
C6H5−CH3 + CrO2Cl2 → [C6H5CH(OCrOHCl)2] (complex) → H2O/H3O+ → C6H5CHO + Cr(OH)2Cl2
Etard reaction is thus used to oxidise a methyl group directly attached to a benzene ring to an aldehyde group.

The product is methylcyclohexane (cyclohexane ring with a CH3 group). This is a classic Clemmensen reduction that converts an aldehyde or ketone to the corresponding hydrocarbon by replacing the C=O group with CH2.

sub_questions.text_english: Calculate the electrode potential of a half-cell for zinc electrode dipping in 0·01 M ZnSO4 solution at 25°C. Given: E°(Zn^2+/Zn) = −0·76 V, log 10 = 1

key_points: Using Nernst equation: E = E° − (0.0591/n) × log(1/[Zn^2+])

sub_questions.solution:
For the half-cell reaction: Zn^2+ + 2e^− → Zn, n = 2.

Nernst equation: E = E° − (0.0591/n) × log(1/[Zn^2+])

E = −0.76 − (0.0591/2) × log(1/0.01)
= −0.76 − (0.02955) × log(10^2)
= −0.76 − (0.02955) × 2 × log 10
= −0.76 − (0.02955) × 2 × 1   [given log 10 = 1]
= −0.76 − 0.0591
= −0.8191 V

The electrode potential of the zinc half-cell is −0.82 V (approximately).

sub_questions.text: शुष्क सेल में होने वाली ऐनोड, कैथोड एवं समग्र अभिक्रिया लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write anode, cathode and overall reaction involved in dry cell.

key_points: Anode: Zn → Zn^2+ + 2e^−
Cathode: MnO2 + NH4+ + e^− → MnO(OH) + NH3
Overall: Zn + 2MnO2 + 2NH4Cl → ZnCl2 + Mn2O3 + 2NH3 + H2O

sub_questions.solution:
In a dry cell (Leclanché cell):

Anode (oxidation): Zn → Zn^2+ + 2e^−

Cathode (reduction): 2MnO2 + 2NH4+ + 2e^− → Mn2O3 + 2NH3 + H2O

Overall reaction: Zn + 2MnO2 + 2NH4Cl → ZnCl2 + Mn2O3 + 2NH3 + H2O

(The zinc anode is consumed, and manganese dioxide is reduced at the cathode, which is a graphite rod surrounded by a paste of MnO2 and NH4Cl.)

sub_questions.text: साम्य स्थिरांक (Kc), E°सेल से तो संबंधित है, परन्तु Eसेल से नहीं। क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: Equilibrium constant (Kc) is related to E°cell, but not to Ecell. Why ?

key_points: Kc is related to the standard free energy change: ΔG° = −nFE°cell = −RT ln Kc. At equilibrium, Ecell = 0 (not E°cell). E°cell represents the cell potential under standard conditions and is a constant for a given reaction.

sub_questions.solution:
The relationship between equilibrium constant and cell potential comes from thermodynamics: ΔG° = −nFE°cell and ΔG° = −RT ln Kc. Therefore, ln Kc = nFE°cell/RT, which means Kc is related to E°cell (the standard cell potential, measured under standard conditions of 1 M, 1 atm, 25°C).

Ecell, however, is the cell potential under non-standard conditions and changes as the reaction proceeds (it depends on the actual concentrations of reactants and products via the Nernst equation). At equilibrium, the reaction quotient Q = Kc, and Ecell becomes zero (no driving force). Since Kc is fixed for a given temperature, it can only be related to the fixed, standard value E°cell — not to the variable Ecell.

sub_questions.text: 0·001 M ऐसीटिक अम्ल विलयन की चालकता 3·905 × 10^−5 S cm^−1 है। इसकी मोलर चालकता एवं वियोजन मात्रा (α) परिकलित कीजिए। λ°(CH3COO^−) = 40·9 S cm^2 mol^−1, λ°(H+) = 349·6 S cm^2 mol^−1
sub_questions.text_english: The conductivity of 0·001 M solution of acetic acid is 3·905 × 10^−5 S cm^−1. Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation (α). Given: λ°(CH3COO^−) = 40·9 S cm^2 mol^−1, λ°(H+) = 349·6 S cm^2 mol^−1
sub_questions.solution:
Step 1 — Molar conductivity:
Λm = (κ × 1000) / c = (3.905 × 10^−5 × 1000) / 0.001 = 3.905 × 10^−2 / 0.001 = 39.05 S cm^2 mol^−1

Step 2 — Limiting molar conductivity of acetic acid (using Kohlrausch's law):
Λ°m(CH3COOH) = λ°(CH3COO^−) + λ°(H+) = 40.9 + 349.6 = 390.5 S cm^2 mol^−1

Step 3 — Degree of dissociation:
α = Λm / Λ°m = 39.05 / 390.5 = 0.1

Therefore, the molar conductivity is 39.05 S cm^2 mol^−1 and the degree of dissociation (α) is 0.1, i.e., 10%.

sub_questions.text: मर्कूरी सेल अपनी संपूर्ण कार्य अवधि में स्थिर वोल्टता क्यों प्रदान करता है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why does a mercury cell deliver a constant voltage for its entire life ?

key_points: In a mercury cell, the overall cell reaction does not involve any ion in solution, so the electrolyte composition (and hence the EMF) does not change during discharge.

sub_questions.solution: A mercury cell delivers a constant voltage throughout its life because the cell reaction does not involve any ion whose concentration changes during operation. The anode reaction is: Zn(Hg) + 2OH^− → ZnO + H2O + 2e^−, and the cathode reaction is: HgO + H2O + 2e^− → Hg + 2OH^−. The OH^− ions consumed at the anode are regenerated at the cathode, keeping the electrolyte composition constant. Since the EMF of a cell depends on the concentrations of reacting species (Nernst equation), a constant concentration means a constant cell potential throughout the entire discharge life.

sub_questions.text: गैल्वेनी सेल में लवण सेतु का उपयोग करना क्यों आवश्यक है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is it necessary to use salt bridge in a galvanic cell ?

key_points: Salt bridge maintains electrical neutrality in both half-cells by allowing migration of ions, and it completes the internal circuit to allow sustained current flow.

sub_questions.solution: A salt bridge is necessary in a galvanic cell for two reasons: (1) It completes the internal circuit by allowing ions to flow between the two half-cells, thereby sustaining the flow of electric current. Without it, the circuit would be broken and no current would flow. (2) It maintains electrical neutrality in both half-cells: as Zn^2+ ions are produced in the anode compartment (becoming positively charged), anions from the salt bridge migrate there to neutralise the charge; simultaneously, as metal ions are deposited at the cathode (becoming negatively charged from excess anions), cations from the salt bridge migrate there. This prevents charge build-up that would otherwise stop the cell reaction.
